Action Plan:
1) Febrile illness after recent travel:
- Same-day in-person evaluation booked at the central London clinic; admin team to arrange. Patient to call the number left in the consultation note to confirm the slot.
- Physical examination on arrival; the examining GP will determine urgency of labs based on findings.
- Blood tests to be arranged after exam: malaria thick and thin blood films; inflammatory markers and general blood tests (specific panels not documented).
- If unable to attend central London today, attend the local emergency department (A&E) and show this note so clinicians can consider the above tests and assessment.

2) Chronic back pain (posture-related):
- Continue ongoing physiotherapy as currently arranged (no new changes discussed today).

3) Headache/migraine history:
- No acute change; no specific intervention discussed today.

4) Fitness for work:
- Do not attend work until assessment and investigations are completed and the cause of fever is clarified.

Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: 7 days of fever with alternating hot/cold episodes, night sweats, diffuse myalgias, nausea, poor appetite, reduced fluid intake, fatigue.
- Symptom modifiers: OTC ibuprofen and paracetamol (recommended doses) provide only partial, temporary relief.
- Negatives: No cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, new/worsening headache, rash, joint swelling, dysuria, urinary frequency.
- Travel: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; multi-week trip including rural trekking/cycling in farmland and city visits. Took daily malaria prophylaxis (drug name unknown); recalls taking “another one” on top of the first (details unclear).
- Past medical history: Chronic back pain (posture/desk-related; in physiotherapy). History of headaches/migraines related to screen use and weather changes.
- Medications:
  - Paroxetine (Seroxat) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Paracetamol OTC — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Ibuprofen OTC — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Seasonal/pollen (hay fever). No medication allergies reported.
- Family history: Father had fatal myocardial infarction at age 68.
- Social: Nurse; up to date on vaccinations including Hepatitis B; non-smoker; moderate alcohol intake; moderate exercise several times per week. Currently struggling to work due to fatigue.

Objective:
- Mode: Teleconsultation; no in-person exam performed.
- Vitals: Not obtained.
- Physical exam: Not performed.
- Investigations: None completed yet. Plan for malaria thick and thin blood films; inflammatory markers and general blood tests (details not specified).

Assessment & Plan:
1. Febrile illness with chills/sweats and myalgias, 7 days, post-travel from Vietnam:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Malaria (High likelihood per DDx).
   - Differential diagnosis (consistent with DDx):
     - Enteric fever (typhoid/paratyphoid) — Medium likelihood.
     - Common viral syndrome (e.g., influenza or COVID-19) — Medium likelihood.
     - Dengue fever — Low-Medium likelihood.
     - Leptospirosis — Low likelihood.
   - Investigations planned:
     - Same-day in-person exam at clinic (or ED if clinic attendance not possible).
     - Malaria thick and thin blood films.
     - Inflammatory markers and general blood tests (specific tests not documented).
   - Treatment planned:
     - No empiric therapy initiated during this teleconsultation; management to be guided by in-person assessment and results.
   - Relevant referrals:
     - Central London clinic for urgent in-person evaluation; alternative: local emergency department (A&E).

2. Chronic back pain (posture-related):
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Chronic mechanical back pain.
   - Differential diagnosis: Not discussed.
   - Investigations planned: None discussed today.
   - Treatment planned: Continue current physiotherapy program (already in place).
   - Relevant referrals: None discussed today.

3. Headache/migraine history:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Stable intermittent tension-type headache/migraine history.
   - Differential diagnosis: Not discussed for this visit.
   - Investigations planned: None discussed.
   - Treatment planned: None discussed.
   - Relevant referrals: None.

4. Fitness for work:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Occupational advice needed due to systemic illness.
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable.
   - Investigations planned: As above for febrile illness.
   - Treatment planned: Advise not to attend work until assessed and cause of fever is clarified.
   - Relevant referrals: None. Work excuse/fit note status not documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals and full physical exam not performed (teleconsult).
  - Pregnancy status/LMP not documented.
  - Specific lab panels beyond malaria films and “inflammatory markers” not detailed.
  - Name of malaria prophylaxis not documented.
  - COVID-19 testing/vaccination status not discussed.
  - Doses/routes/frequencies for medications not documented.
  - Safety net advice/return precautions not explicitly documented.
  - Work excuse/fit note not documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Patient initially denied migraines, later stated occasional migraines related to weather/screen use (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some pauses/overlap and minor inaudible segments; no objective measurements available due to teleconsult format.
